## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. 1	# Backlog
2	
3	The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
4	refactoring. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the full
5	detail (smell, effort, sibling sites, plan) lives in
6	[Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a reference, not a
7	separate to-do list.
8	
9	## Features
10	
11	- **Spending Report (v1).** New top-level `/spending` tab rolling up Expenses by Importance → Grouping → Category, months across, "Year to Date" total. Adds `importance_areas` + `category_groups` tables (Importance attaches to the Grouping) and `categories.group_id`, seeded from `docs/SampleHierachy.txt`. Client-side pure aggregation (`buildSpendingReport`), view-only, no editing UI. Uncategorized bucket included in Grand Total; refunds (negative amounts) net against spend. **Chart view (v0.60):** `Table | Chart` toggle adds a LayerChart stacked bar (bar per Grouping, stacked by month, sequential ramp; Importance as sub-label; click a bar to drill to Categories, breadcrumb back). Pure `buildSpendingChart`; render-tested. **Table cell drill-down (v0.55) ✅ DONE:** clicking a non-blank table cell opens `/expenses` filtered to exactly what it sums — category×month, category YTD, Grouping/Importance subtotals (expanded to member category ids), Uncategorized (`filter=uncategorized`), and Grand Total (date range only, ties out incl. Uncategorized). Pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` (8 tests); report rows/sections now carry ids (`categoryId`/group `id`/importance `id`). **Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent (v0.65) ✅ DONE:** an **Edit hierarchy** page at `/spending/hierarchy` (button on `/spending`) lets the maintainer assign a Category to a Grouping (or Uncategorized) and move a Grouping to another Importance — closing the "custom/renamed categories stuck in Uncategorized" gap without SQL. Pure `buildHierarchyTree` (8 tests) + presentational `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (5 render tests); `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup` / `moveGroupToImportance`. Unassigned bucket surfaced up top. **Assign-on-create (v0.66) ✅ DONE:** the inline "Create new category…" form (expenses page `CategoryDropdown`) offers an optional Group selector so a new category is filed into a Grouping at birth instead of Uncategorized (`createCategory` gained an optional `groupId`; selector hidden when no groups passed, so receipt/reconciliation dropdowns are unchanged). **Historical-year expense upload (built, pending release) ✅ DONE:** an **Import Expenses** page at `/expenses/import` (buttons on `/expenses` and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from CSV/XLS/XLSX (columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category`; `Tag` ignored; Amount keeps its sign so refunds net). Each row → an imageless `receipts` row (no schema change — `receipt_image_path` nullable, `suspicious_date` false) + an `expense_categories` link; new category names are auto-created (land Uncategorized, warned in the preview). Two-step **preview → confirm** with count-based dedup (`date|merchant|amount|category`) so re-import is a no-op. Pure `parseExpenseImportCsv` (14) + `computeExpenseImportPlan`/`buildExpenseCategoryLinks` (12) + `ExpenseImportService` (7); the bank-parser CSV primitives were extracted to `csvPrimitives.ts` (base delegates; 229 parser tests unchanged). This **unblocks** prior-period overlay + year-over-year. Deferred: **chart-bar drill-down** (same affordance on the chart bars — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); prior-period overlay + year-over-year (now unblocked), quarter/period selection, multi-chart menu, export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
12	- **Delete a category (built, pending release) ✅ DONE.** Each category row in the hierarchy editor (`/spending/hierarchy`) now has a **Delete** button (`HierarchyEditor.onDeleteCategory`). The page confirms first, surfacing how many expenses are affected: the DB nulls the category on its expenses (`expense_categories.category_id ON DELETE SET NULL`, so history survives → they drop to Uncategorized) and cascade-removes any vendor rules (`vendor_category_rules … ON DELETE CASCADE`) — no blocking, since delete is DB-safe. The existing `CategoryService.deleteCategory` is reused; new `countCategoryExpenses` uses an exact `head` count (not a plain select, which the default 1000-row cap would undercount). Tests: 3 service specs + 2 `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec` render tests.
13	- **Mass-change categories on the expenses page (built, pending release) ✅ DONE.** No dedicated bulk control: once multiple rows are selected (existing `DataTable` select-all/row checkboxes + `expenseSelection`), **picking a category on any selected row's own dropdown fans the change out to the whole selection** (`handleCategorySelect` routes to `applyCategoryToSelection` → `ExpenseService.bulkAssignCategory`, one batched upsert). A single checked row still takes the normal single-row path (keeps vendor-rule auto-creation); the bulk path deliberately skips vendor rules (a multi-row selection spans many merchants). A one-line hint appears while >1 row is selected. Two render tests in `expenses-page.svelte.spec.ts` (fan-out + single-row guard).
14	- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
15	- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account.
16	- **View family members (built, pending release) ✅ DONE.** A read-only **Family Members** section on the Profile page (`/profile`) lists the current user's default-family members by primary email, with **You**/**Owner** badges. Reads through a new `get_family_members()` `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC (`20260719_get_family_members_rpc.sql`) that derives the caller's default family and joins `auth.users` for the email — the only way past RLS, since `auth.users` isn't client-readable and `profiles` emails are owner-scoped; grants revoked from public/anon, granted to `authenticated`. Pure `decorateFamilyMembers` (6 tests) + `getFamilyMembers()`. Read-only slice; the invite/add/remove half stays in the Family Invitations PRD.
17	- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped F1 self-insert policy). The read-only member-list half (D5's roster) shipped separately — see "View family members" above.
18	- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). Also flags a suspected bug worth verifying on-device: the receipts `accept` list includes `image/heic`, which may make iOS hand over a raw HEIC that `resizeImage()` then skips entirely (`imageResize.ts:71`), sending a full-size photo to storage and Mistral on cellular.
19	- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y _(optional UX, low priority)_.** Recent-categories dropdown section (exp2b), mobile-responsive category dropdown (exp8a), and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support (exp8b) were specced but never built.
20	- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits _(optional, low priority)_.** Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (vca2a email path) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal (fcr2b) were specced but not implemented.
21	
22	## Bugs / UX issues
23	
24	- **Receipt with No Date** - if a receipt has no date it is hard to find in the receipts view.
25	- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
26	- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
27	- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is deliberate and locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
28	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
29	- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).
30	
31	## Engineering
32	
33	- **✅ DONE — unauthenticated data-forgery chain closed.** The [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md) shipped R2–R5 in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` (+ follow-up `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql`) and **verified all five §Verification checks against the live deployment on 2026-07-17**: anon `find_user_by_email` (R4/H1) and `insert_receipt_with_context` (R2/C2) denied, `family_members` reads scoped via an `is_member_of()` SECURITY DEFINER helper (R5/H2), tautological receipts INSERT/UPDATE `WITH CHECK` fixed to `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id` (R3/C3), and webhook signature enforced (R1/C1). Verified with the throwaway `.scratch/verify-security.sh` (uncommitted). PRD moved to `docs/prd-done/`.
34	- **✅ DONE — family_members self-join closed.** The open `"Users can insert their own membership"` INSERT policy (which, with the `USING(true)` SELECT, let any authed user self-join any family for a whole-tenant breach) was **dropped** in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`. There is now no client membership-write path — legitimate membership goes through the `SECURITY DEFINER` `ensure_default_family()` (bypasses RLS). Verified live 2026-07-17 (self-insert into an arbitrary family rejected). The sanctioned invite-based replacement is designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md).
35	- **🟠 HIGH SECURITY — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint** (`002_profiles_table.sql`). The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix (abuse is by a legit authed user). Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
36	- **✅ DONE — anon-executable seed functions locked down.** `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` carried a **direct** `anon` EXECUTE grant (Supabase default privileges), so `anon` could seed rows into empty tenants. `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` revoked `FROM PUBLIC`, but live testing showed that missed the direct anon grant (the call still executed, blocked only by a FK) — so `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` added explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`; `authenticated` keeps its grant (the `CategoryService` caller). Verified live 2026-07-17. **Lesson learned:** on Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` alone does NOT remove `anon`/`authenticated` — they hold _direct_ grants via default privileges, so revoke those roles explicitly. (Still open: a sweep of any _other_ `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE.)
37	- **🟢 LOW SECURITY / deferred audit items still open (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Still present, unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF via caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, incl. svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`) — the secret-prefix leak was fixed in the refactor but these two survived; **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes+re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding / no limit). Also **F6:** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject (`20260705_email_send_failures.sql`) — confirm intended. (The `receipts` UPDATE `WITH CHECK` tautology noted here previously is now **fixed** — shipped as part of R3.) The top remaining security item is **F2** (unverified/non-unique profile emails → email-ingestion hijack), tracked as its own High item above.
38	- **Remove the abandoned Spending Bridge (waterfall) view. ✅ DONE.** Built as a 3rd `/spending` view then abandoned as not intuitive — [ADR-0004](adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) (reminder screenshot `docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`). Deleted `SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, and their `.spec.ts`; stripped the `Bridge` toggle, render branch, `'bridge'` view type, and `priorReport` state from `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte`. Full suite green (1424), `check`/eslint/Prettier clean. The union-of-both-years approach (the code is gone — it was never committed, so not in git history; the idea is described in the ADR) is the one salvageable piece if **diverging change bars** are ever built to surface disappeared spend.

# Backlog

The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
refactoring. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the full
detail (smell, effort, sibling sites, plan) lives in
[Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a reference, not a
separate to-do list.

## Features

- **Spending Report (v1).** New top-level `/spending` tab rolling up Expenses by Importance → Grouping → Category, months across, "Year to Date" total. Adds `importance_areas` + `category_groups` tables (Importance attaches to the Grouping) and `categories.group_id`, seeded from `docs/SampleHierachy.txt`. Client-side pure aggregation (`buildSpendingReport`), view-only, no editing UI. Uncategorized bucket included in Grand Total; refunds (negative amounts) net against spend. **Chart view (v0.60):** `Table | Chart` toggle adds a LayerChart stacked bar (bar per Grouping, stacked by month, sequential ramp; Importance as sub-label; click a bar to drill to Categories, breadcrumb back). Pure `buildSpendingChart`; render-tested. **Table cell drill-down (v0.55) ✅ DONE:** clicking a non-blank table cell opens `/expenses` filtered to exactly what it sums — category×month, category YTD, Grouping/Importance subtotals (expanded to member category ids), Uncategorized (`filter=uncategorized`), and Grand Total (date range only, ties out incl. Uncategorized). Pure `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` (8 tests); report rows/sections now carry ids (`categoryId`/group `id`/importance `id`). **Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent (v0.65) ✅ DONE:** an **Edit hierarchy** page at `/spending/hierarchy` (button on `/spending`) lets the maintainer assign a Category to a Grouping (or Uncategorized) and move a Grouping to another Importance — closing the "custom/renamed categories stuck in Uncategorized" gap without SQL. Pure `buildHierarchyTree` (8 tests) + presentational `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (5 render tests); `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup` / `moveGroupToImportance`. Unassigned bucket surfaced up top. **Assign-on-create (v0.66) ✅ DONE:** the inline "Create new category…" form (expenses page `CategoryDropdown`) offers an optional Group selector so a new category is filed into a Grouping at birth instead of Uncategorized (`createCategory` gained an optional `groupId`; selector hidden when no groups passed, so receipt/reconciliation dropdowns are unchanged). **Historical-year expense upload (built, pending release) ✅ DONE:** an **Import Expenses** page at `/expenses/import` (buttons on `/expenses` and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from CSV/XLS/XLSX (columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category`; `Tag` ignored; Amount keeps its sign so refunds net). Each row → an imageless `receipts` row (no schema change — `receipt_image_path` nullable, `suspicious_date` false) + an `expense_categories` link; new category names are auto-created (land Uncategorized, warned in the preview). Two-step **preview → confirm** with count-based dedup (`date|merchant|amount|category`) so re-import is a no-op. Pure `parseExpenseImportCsv` (14) + `computeExpenseImportPlan`/`buildExpenseCategoryLinks` (12) + `ExpenseImportService` (7); the bank-parser CSV primitives were extracted to `csvPrimitives.ts` (base delegates; 229 parser tests unchanged). This **unblocks** prior-period overlay + year-over-year. Deferred: **chart-bar drill-down** (same affordance on the chart bars — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); prior-period overlay + year-over-year (now unblocked), quarter/period selection, multi-chart menu, export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
- **Delete a category (built, pending release) ✅ DONE.** Each category row in the hierarchy editor (`/spending/hierarchy`) now has a **Delete** button (`HierarchyEditor.onDeleteCategory`). The page confirms first, surfacing how many expenses are affected: the DB nulls the category on its expenses (`expense_categories.category_id ON DELETE SET NULL`, so history survives → they drop to Uncategorized) and cascade-removes any vendor rules (`vendor_category_rules … ON DELETE CASCADE`) — no blocking, since delete is DB-safe. The existing `CategoryService.deleteCategory` is reused; new `countCategoryExpenses` uses an exact `head` count (not a plain select, which the default 1000-row cap would undercount). Tests: 3 service specs + 2 `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec` render tests.
- **Mass-change categories on the expenses page (built, pending release) ✅ DONE.** No dedicated bulk control: once multiple rows are selected (existing `DataTable` select-all/row checkboxes + `expenseSelection`), **picking a category on any selected row's own dropdown fans the change out to the whole selection** (`handleCategorySelect` routes to `applyCategoryToSelection` → `ExpenseService.bulkAssignCategory`, one batched upsert). A single checked row still takes the normal single-row path (keeps vendor-rule auto-creation); the bulk path deliberately skips vendor rules (a multi-row selection spans many merchants). A one-line hint appears while >1 row is selected. Two render tests in `expenses-page.svelte.spec.ts` (fan-out + single-row guard).
- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account.
- **View family members (built, pending release) ✅ DONE.** A read-only **Family Members** section on the Profile page (`/profile`) lists the current user's default-family members by primary email, with **You**/**Owner** badges. Reads through a new `get_family_members()` `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC (`20260719_get_family_members_rpc.sql`) that derives the caller's default family and joins `auth.users` for the email — the only way past RLS, since `auth.users` isn't client-readable and `profiles` emails are owner-scoped; grants revoked from public/anon, granted to `authenticated`. Pure `decorateFamilyMembers` (6 tests) + `getFamilyMembers()`. Read-only slice; the invite/add/remove half stays in the Family Invitations PRD.
- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped F1 self-insert policy). The read-only member-list half (D5's roster) shipped separately — see "View family members" above.
- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). Also flags a suspected bug worth verifying on-device: the receipts `accept` list includes `image/heic`, which may make iOS hand over a raw HEIC that `resizeImage()` then skips entirely (`imageResize.ts:71`), sending a full-size photo to storage and Mistral on cellular.
- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y _(optional UX, low priority)_.** Recent-categories dropdown section (exp2b), mobile-responsive category dropdown (exp8a), and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support (exp8b) were specced but never built.
- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits _(optional, low priority)_.** Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (vca2a email path) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal (fcr2b) were specced but not implemented.

## Bugs / UX issues

- **Receipt with No Date** - if a receipt has no date it is hard to find in the receipts view.
- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is deliberate and locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

## Engineering

- **✅ DONE — unauthenticated data-forgery chain closed.** The [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md) shipped R2–R5 in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` (+ follow-up `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql`) and **verified all five §Verification checks against the live deployment on 2026-07-17**: anon `find_user_by_email` (R4/H1) and `insert_receipt_with_context` (R2/C2) denied, `family_members` reads scoped via an `is_member_of()` SECURITY DEFINER helper (R5/H2), tautological receipts INSERT/UPDATE `WITH CHECK` fixed to `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id` (R3/C3), and webhook signature enforced (R1/C1). Verified with the throwaway `.scratch/verify-security.sh` (uncommitted). PRD moved to `docs/prd-done/`.
- **✅ DONE — family_members self-join closed.** The open `"Users can insert their own membership"` INSERT policy (which, with the `USING(true)` SELECT, let any authed user self-join any family for a whole-tenant breach) was **dropped** in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`. There is now no client membership-write path — legitimate membership goes through the `SECURITY DEFINER` `ensure_default_family()` (bypasses RLS). Verified live 2026-07-17 (self-insert into an arbitrary family rejected). The sanctioned invite-based replacement is designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md).
- **🟠 HIGH SECURITY — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint** (`002_profiles_table.sql`). The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix (abuse is by a legit authed user). Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **✅ DONE — anon-executable seed functions locked down.** `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` carried a **direct** `anon` EXECUTE grant (Supabase default privileges), so `anon` could seed rows into empty tenants. `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` revoked `FROM PUBLIC`, but live testing showed that missed the direct anon grant (the call still executed, blocked only by a FK) — so `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` added explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`; `authenticated` keeps its grant (the `CategoryService` caller). Verified live 2026-07-17. **Lesson learned:** on Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` alone does NOT remove `anon`/`authenticated` — they hold _direct_ grants via default privileges, so revoke those roles explicitly. (Still open: a sweep of any _other_ `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE.)
- **🟢 LOW SECURITY / deferred audit items still open (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Still present, unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF via caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, incl. svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`) — the secret-prefix leak was fixed in the refactor but these two survived; **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes+re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding / no limit). Also **F6:** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject (`20260705_email_send_failures.sql`) — confirm intended. (The `receipts` UPDATE `WITH CHECK` tautology noted here previously is now **fixed** — shipped as part of R3.) The top remaining security item is **F2** (unverified/non-unique profile emails → email-ingestion hijack), tracked as its own High item above.
- **Remove the abandoned Spending Bridge (waterfall) view. ✅ DONE.** Built as a 3rd `/spending` view then abandoned as not intuitive — [ADR-0004](adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) (reminder screenshot `docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`). Deleted `SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, and their `.spec.ts`; stripped the `Bridge` toggle, render branch, `'bridge'` view type, and `priorReport` state from `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte`. Full suite green (1424), `check`/eslint/Prettier clean. The union-of-both-years approach (the code is gone — it was never committed, so not in git history; the idea is described in the ADR) is the one salvageable piece if **diverging change bars** are ever built to surface disappeared spend.
- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), CVE-2023-30533, fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), CVE-2024-22363, fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist but **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there's no fix version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, fully contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` (`convertExcelToCSV`/`isExcelFile`, ~4 API calls) behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx` (tests build both, `ExcelToCSVConverter.test.ts`). Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.
- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie` rather than force it. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix` (non-breaking). Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.
- **Expenses list capped at 1000 rows (large imports). ✅ DONE.** `ExpenseService.getExpenses` issued a single PostgREST query with no paging, so Supabase's default 1000-row cap silently truncated the result. After the historical importer added thousands of receipts, the expenses page (which loads all expenses then filters client-side) only held the newest 1000 — a Spending-report drill-down into an older year landed on "No results found — hiding all 1000 expenses", and the Spending report itself undercounted any year over 1000 rows. Fixed by paging `getExpenses` in 1000-row `.range()` batches until a short page (`fetchAllReceiptRows`); the shared Supabase mock gained `range`; 2 new pagination tests in `ExpenseService.getExpenses.spec.ts`. Reported via a `/spending` uncategorized drill-down.
- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That's the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the `$page` store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was ultimately fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation off the page store did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern to the expenses date filter (and audit any other `$derived(... $page.url ...)` sites). Not yet reproduced/reported for expenses — latent. See the Spending report design doc and the URL-backed-state note.
- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (`supabase/migrations/003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, and again in `20251010000319_remote_schema.sql`). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path (they only survive if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback). Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert (new migration) and confirm the remote function matches. Found while fixing the email-receipt null-date bug.
- **Test the Resend webhook handler. ✅ DONE.** `handleResendWebhook(req, deps)` extracted from `Deno.serve` into `supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts` (functional core) with `index.ts` reduced to the dep-wiring shell; `notify.ts` / `mistral.ts` / `exchangeRate.ts` gained optional `fetchFn`/`env` seams. The full branch matrix (rows 1–20: auth gates, body/attachment/fallback flow, notify-on-failure, foreign-currency) is covered in `handler.test.ts` (20 vitest cases, no network/Supabase/Deno). `deno check` clean on all production files. See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-done/prd-resend-handler-testability.md).
- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for row 18 (nothing found anywhere), but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case (row 10). The tests assert the real `422` (zero-behaviour-change goal); the PRD table row is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the PRD table or leave the note.
- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle (umf1a/2a/3a) was specced but never built. Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.
- **Manually verify ReceiptImageViewer gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests only cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
- **`npm run lint` is fully green. ✅ DONE.** `npm run lint` (`prettier --check . && eslint .`) passes with exit 0 across the whole repo. Prettier: the repo is clean (`llm_history/`, a chat-log archive, added to `.prettierignore`). ESLint: triaged from 46 → 0. Verified with `deno check` (both edited source files type-check clean). ## The local-only guard

`readConfig()` rejects any `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` whose hostname is not loopback,
before the service-role client is built. That is what makes a checked-in
password acceptable: seeding a remote project would plant a known credential in
it, so "don't do that" is enforced rather than agreed. Relaxing the guard means
reinstating a generated password.

A full local wipe is `npm run db:reset` — `seed:demo:teardown` exists for
removing just the demo family while leaving the rest of your local data intact.

`seed:demo` is **auto-clean-then-recreate**: it runs the teardown first, so every
run yields the same known-good state. Deletion is scoped strictly to the two
demo emails and the `Sample Family (DEMO)` name, so it can only ever touch demo
artifacts — never your real data (which lives under a different `family_id` and
stays invisible to the demo login via RLS, and vice-versa).

## What it creates

- **Two auth users** (owner + member), one shared **family**, with the app's own
  **default categories + spending hierarchy** — categories via `CategoryService`
  (the same `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` list a real new family gets, so the demo tracks
  it as it is refined), the hierarchy via the `create_default_hierarchy` RPC.
- **~150 receipts** spread across **all of 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026**, ~6–8 per month,
  split across both users and most of the 13 default groupings / 3 Areas of
  Importance — enough to fill the Spending grid, YTD, and the compare-to-prior-year
  toggle.
- **~95 transactions**, most matched 1:1 to a receipt (equal amount, date within
  3 days), the rest unmatched on each side.
- **One instance of every notable edge state**, planted in recent months so it's
  visible without scrolling: split receipt, matched pair, unmatched (both sides),
  duplicate pair, suspicious/old date, future-dated ("Upcoming"), refund/credit,
  excluded transaction, amount-not-read (null total), foreign currency (USD), and
  uncategorized.

The dataset is generated deterministically (fixed RNG seed), so reseeding
produces the same data and screenshots stay stable.

## The no-image consequence

Because no receipt has an image, every screen shows its empty/placeholder state:
the Expenses page shows a column of grey "No image" boxes, the Receipts page has
blank thumbnail cells, and Reconciliation tags every receipt "(manual)". This is
intentional. If a screenshot ever needs the receipt-image viewer itself, seed a
few receipts with real placeholder images (a small change to `scripts/demo/data.ts`).

## Files

- `scripts/demo/common.ts` — env guard, service-role client, teardown.
- `scripts/demo/data.ts` — pure, deterministic dataset generator (no DB access).
- `scripts/demo/seed.ts` — orchestrates users → family → categories → data.
- `scripts/demo/teardown.ts` — standalone teardown entrypoint.

Run via `tsx` (added as a dev dependency).

76	- Multi-email support: primary email in `auth.users`, up to 5 additional in `profiles` table. Email receipt ingestion checks both.
77	- File uploads: JPEG/PNG/HEIC up to 5MB, PDF up to 10MB. Validated client-side and server-side (`src/lib/server/fileValidation.ts`)
78	- Recent migrations (Jan–Feb 2026) refactored family-scoping, fixed RLS recursion issues, and secured storage — be careful modifying RLS policies

+- On Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` does **not** remove `anon` / `authenticated` — those roles hold _direct_ grants via default privileges, so revoke each role explicitly. A function can look locked down and still be anon-executable.

+- PostgREST caps every query at **1000 rows by default**, silently. Any list that can exceed that must page in `.range()` batches until a short page (see `ExpenseService.getExpenses`), and any count must use an exact `head` count rather than a plain select's `.length`.

+- Regenerating `.svelte-kit` does **not** update the root `tsconfig.json` `include`. The root config restates the generated list plus `scripts/**/*.ts` and `e2e/**/*.ts` (it replaces rather than merges), so `npm run check` covers them; if SvelteKit ever adds an entry, copy it across by hand. `supabase/functions/` stays out of scope (Deno — verify with `deno check`).

+- `.env` is a **FIFO**, so nothing can read it twice. `npm run dev` works only because `op run --env-file=.env` consumes the named pipe and injects the values; a bare `vite build`, a second reader, or any tool expecting a regular file gets nothing. This is why `playwright.config.ts` hard-codes fake public config and the local scripts inline Supabase's well-known local defaults.

+- Test harness: `src/lib/tests/harness/appMocks.ts` (+ `LayoutHarness.svelte`) mocks the SvelteKit + Supabase boundaries so real `+page.svelte` / `+layout.svelte` render in the `client` project (`setRoute`/`setSession`/`setReceipts`/… plus service stubs). The canonical chainable Supabase mock is `src/lib/tests/fixtures/supabaseMock.ts`; row builders in `rowBuilders.ts`; fetch stubs in `fixtures/fetchMock.ts`. Prefer these over a local copy — and when auditing for tests that reimplement production logic, look for logic inlined _inside_ `it()` bodies, not just `function`-defined helpers.

- `overflow-x-auto` clips dropdowns in BOTH axes: a wrapper whose `overflow-x` is non-visible has its computed `overflow-y` become `auto` (not `visible`), so `overflow-x-auto` on a table wrapper clips absolutely-positioned dropdown menus vertically too. Keep the expenses table wrapper free of it; position menus with `right-0`.

Two failure modes: format-ambiguity (auto-fixable) vs wrong-token extraction (only flaggable). Ruled out — do not reintroduce: prompt-tuning date interpretation, using the matched bank-transaction date as truth (circular), extracting all date tokens. `raw_date_text` is transient (never persisted); the `supabase/functions/_shared/` Deno copy of the correction logic must stay in lock-step with `src/lib/utils/`.

- Password policy: 16-char minimum (NIST length-over-complexity), at least one of upper/lower/number/special, exact confirmation match (whitespace-preserving, case-sensitive). Constants/messages exported from `src/lib/utils/passwordValidation.ts`.

# Demo Data Seed

A re-runnable script that populates a self-contained **"Sample Family (DEMO)"**
in the **local** Supabase stack, so the running app can be logged into for
documentation screenshots/videos and manual exploratory testing.

> **Local only.** The demo family was also seeded into the remote project until
> 2026-07-26, when it was torn down there and the remote scripts were removed.
> `readConfig()` now refuses any non-loopback target.

It is deliberately **image-free**: every seeded receipt has
`receipt_image_path = null`, so receipts render in their placeholder state
("No image" / "(manual)"). See the note on that below.

> **Reuse:** the seed is written so a future automated test harness can reuse
> the same fixtures. That harness is **not** built yet — this is a dev utility
> today.

## Logins

| Role   | Email                        |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| Owner  | `sample.parent@example.com`  |
| Member | `sample.partner@example.com` |

Both share one family and one **fixed password**, `DEMO_PASSWORD` in
`scripts/demo/common.ts`, also printed at the end of each seed run.
`@example.com` is an IANA-reserved documentation domain — it accepts no mail and
can't collide with real accounts.

The password used to be randomly generated per run. It is a checked-in constant
now so local tooling can log in unattended, which is only safe because the demo
account cannot exist anywhere but a loopback stack — see the guard below.

## Commands

```bash
npm run seed:demo            # auto-clean any prior demo data, then rebuild
npm run seed:demo:teardown   # delete the demo users + demo family
```

Both wrap `local:env`, which injects Supabase's fixed local defaults, so neither
needs 1Password. They need:

- `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` — the target stack (echoed on start).
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — full-access key; required to create the auth
  users (Admin API) and to insert RLS-protected rows. The scripts hard-fail with
  a clear message if either is missing.

## The local-only guard

`readConfig()` rejects any `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` whose hostname is not loopback,
before the service-role client is built. That is what makes a checked-in
password acceptable: seeding a remote project would plant a known credential in
it, so "don't do that" is enforced rather than agreed. Relaxing the guard means
reinstating a generated password.

A full local wipe is `npm run db:reset` — `seed:demo:teardown` exists for
removing just the demo family while leaving the rest of your local data intact.

`seed:demo` is **auto-clean-then-recreate**: it runs the teardown first, so every
run yields the same known-good state. Deletion is scoped strictly to the two
demo emails and the `Sample Family (DEMO)` name, so it can only ever touch demo
artifacts — never your real data (which lives under a different `family_id` and
stays invisible to the demo login via RLS, and vice-versa).

## What it creates

- **Two auth users** (owner + member), one shared **family**, with the app's own
  **default categories + spending hierarchy** — categories via `CategoryService`
  (the same `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` list a real new family gets, so the demo tracks
  it as it is refined), the hierarchy via the `create_default_hierarchy` RPC.
- **~150 receipts** spread across **all of 2025 + Jan–Jul 2026**, ~6–8 per month,
  split across both users and most of the 13 default groupings / 3 Areas of
  Importance — enough to fill the Spending grid, YTD, and the compare-to-prior-year
  toggle.
- **~95 transactions**, most matched 1:1 to a receipt (equal amount, date within
  3 days), the rest unmatched on each side.
- **One instance of every notable edge state**, planted in recent months so it's
  visible without scrolling: split receipt, matched pair, unmatched (both sides),
  duplicate pair, suspicious/old date, future-dated ("Upcoming"), refund/credit,
  excluded transaction, amount-not-read (null total), foreign currency (USD), and
  uncategorized.

The dataset is generated deterministically (fixed RNG seed), so reseeding
produces the same data and screenshots stay stable.

## The no-image consequence

Because no receipt has an image, every screen shows its empty/placeholder state:
the Expenses page shows a column of grey "No image" boxes, the Receipts page has
blank thumbnail cells, and Reconciliation tags every receipt "(manual)". This is
intentional. If a screenshot ever needs the receipt-image viewer itself, seed a
few receipts with real placeholder images (a small change to `scripts/demo/data.ts`).

## Files

- `scripts/demo/common.ts` — env guard, service-role client, teardown.
- `scripts/demo/data.ts` — pure, deterministic dataset generator (no DB access).
- `scripts/demo/seed.ts` — orchestrates users → family → categories → data.
- `scripts/demo/teardown.ts` — standalone teardown entrypoint.

Run via `tsx` (added as a dev dependency).

# Backlog

The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
refactoring. Everything here is **open**: something a person could pick up.

**Completed work is deleted from this file, not annotated.** History lives in git,
in [ADRs](adr/) for decisions and rejected paths, in [`prd-done/`](prd-done/) for
finished PRDs, and in `CLAUDE.md` for anything that stays true and will bite
someone later. When an item lands, salvage any durable lesson into one of those
and remove the bullet. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the
full detail lives in [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a
reference, not a separate to-do list.

## Features

- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy, assign-on-create, and historical-expense import are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same drill affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** (unblocked now that historical years can be imported); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. Note this interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.
- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.
- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). Also flags a suspected bug worth verifying on-device: the receipts `accept` list includes `image/heic`, which may make iOS hand over a raw HEIC that `resizeImage()` then skips entirely (`imageResize.ts:71`), sending a full-size photo to storage and Mistral on cellular.
- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.
- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (the email path never got the vendor rule applied) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.

## Bugs / UX issues

- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

## Engineering

### Security

- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a *direct* `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes and re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

### Dependencies

- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

### Correctness / infrastructure

- **Add a CI pipeline with a required `npm run check` gate.** The [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-done/prd-type-check-cleanup.md) got `npm run check` to 0 errors / 0 warnings (down from 118), but its second goal — making the type check a _required CI gate so it can't silently regress_ — is unmet: the repo has **no CI at all** (`.github/workflows/` does not exist). Without a gate the green state will rot exactly as before. Stand up a workflow (GitHub Actions is the natural fit) running at least `npm run check` on every PR and blocking merge on failure; fold in `npm run lint` and `npm test` while there. CI installs must use `npm ci` (honours the lockfile; `min-release-age` gates resolution, not `ci`). This is the last open deliverable of that PRD.
- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (`003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That is the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern here, and audit any other `$derived(… $page.url …)` site. Latent — not yet reproduced for expenses.
- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced but never built. **Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.**
- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.

## Refactoring

No open items. Every catalogued refactoring (**RF-01→13**, plus code-review
follow-ups **RV-01→11**) has landed — see [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md)
for the per-item Landed notes. The only outstanding entries are the two deferred
value-object questions, **RF-D1** (`Money`) and **RF-D2** (typed date) — both a
recorded _keep-primitives_ decision, not scheduled work. New refactoring ideas start
here as one-liners and get promoted to an `RF-NN` entry only when work begins.

## Open questions

- **Combining receipts for one expense.** How to handle when two receipts should be combined into one expense to match — e.g. two medications picked up at the same time.
- **WealthSimple refund handling.** WealthSimple records several rows when a refund is issued. Example:

  ```csv
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-24","Refund initiated","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
  ```
