# Backlog

The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
refactoring. Everything here is **open**: something a person could pick up.

**Completed work is deleted from this file, not annotated.** History lives in git,
in [ADRs](adr/) for decisions and rejected paths, in [`prd-done/`](prd-done/) for
finished PRDs, and in `CLAUDE.md` for anything that stays true and will bite
someone later. When an item lands, salvage any durable lesson into one of those
and remove the bullet. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the
full detail lives in [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a
reference, not a separate to-do list.

## Features

- **Spending Report — remaining slices.** The report ships: table + chart views, cell drill-down, editable hierarchy, assign-on-create, and historical-expense import are all live. Still open, roughly in priority order: **chart-bar drill-down** (the same drill affordance the table cells have — carry the cell-link into `/expenses` from a bar/bracket click); **hierarchy tier CRUD** (create/rename/delete/reorder Groupings + Importance areas, with cascade-delete confirmations); **prior-period overlay + year-over-year** (unblocked now that historical years can be imported); quarter/period selection; multi-chart menu; export. See [Spending Report design](plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md).
- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.
- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.
- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). Also flags a suspected bug worth verifying on-device: the receipts `accept` list includes `image/heic`, which may make iOS hand over a raw HEIC that `resizeImage()` then skips entirely (`imageResize.ts:71`), sending a full-size photo to storage and Mistral on cellular.
- **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.
- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (the email path never applies the vendor rule) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.

## Bugs / UX issues

- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). See [Email notifications — scenario 7](email-notifications.md).

## Engineering

### In progress

- **🟡 Bombadil property-based UI testing (spike).** Researched and scoped 2026-07-26; prerequisites landed, nothing Bombadil-specific built. Feasible against the local stack with all three constraints met (local-only, single page, no Mistral), but two of them can't be met through Bombadil's own config: `<ORIGIN>` bounds navigation at the **origin**, not the path, so single-page scoping has to be done in the spec; and there is **no network mocking**, so Mistral is avoided by page choice plus running with no `MISTRAL_API_KEY`. Auth is undocumented at v0.6.1 and the session lives in localStorage, so the plan is a DEV-and-loopback-gated auto-login rather than `test-external`. Target page `/transactions`. Remaining: `src/lib/dev/autoLogin.ts` + layout hook, `db:fresh`, and the specification file. See [Bombadil spike handoff](plans/2026-07-26-bombadil-property-testing-spike.md).

### Security

- **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes and re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()`; **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

### Dependencies

- **High vuln: `xlsx` (SheetJS) has no npm fix — decision needed.** `npm audit` reports 1 high against `xlsx@^0.18.5` — Prototype Pollution ([GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4r6h-8v6p-xvw6), fixed in 0.19.3) and ReDoS ([GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5pgg-2g8v-p4x9), fixed in 0.20.2). Both fixes exist **only on the SheetJS CDN (`cdn.sheetjs.com`), not npm** — the npm package is unmaintained, so `npm audit` will never clear and there is no version to bump to. Used only by the Excel importer, contained in `src/lib/services/ExcelToCSVConverter.ts` behind a stable interface; the app supports **both** legacy `.xls` (BIFF8) and `.xlsx`. Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball via `overrides` — clears the CVEs and keeps `.xls`, but adds a non-registry dep our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`**, so it drops that support unless paired with a BIFF parser. **The decision to make: is legacy `.xls` still required?** Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers practical risk.
- **Low vulns: `cookie` (via `@sveltejs/kit`) and `esbuild` dev server.** `npm audit` reports 6 low-severity issues. (1) `cookie <0.7.0` accepts out-of-bounds characters in name/path/domain ([GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pxg6-pf52-xh8x)), pulled in transitively through `@sveltejs/kit` → `@sveltejs/adapter-auto` / `runed` / `layerchart`; `npm audit fix --force` would downgrade `@sveltejs/kit` to `1.0.0-next.0` (breaking), so wait for the framework chain to bump `cookie`. (2) `esbuild 0.27.3–0.28.0` allows arbitrary file read when the dev server runs on Windows ([GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)) — dev-only, non-Windows here; clearable with a plain `npm audit fix`. Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

### Correctness / infrastructure

- **Add a CI pipeline with a required `npm run check` gate.** The [type-check-cleanup PRD](prd-done/prd-type-check-cleanup.md) got `npm run check` to 0 errors / 0 warnings (down from 118), but its second goal — making the type check a _required CI gate so it can't silently regress_ — is unmet: the repo has **no CI at all** (`.github/workflows/` does not exist). Without a gate the green state will rot exactly as before. Stand up a workflow (GitHub Actions is the natural fit) running at least `npm run check` on every PR and blocking merge on failure; fold in `npm run lint` and `npm test` while there. CI installs must use `npm ci` (honours the lockfile; `min-release-age` gates resolution, not `ci`). This is the last open deliverable of that PRD.
- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (originally `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
- **Expenses page: date filter may go stale on Back nav (legacy `$page` store).** `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte` derives its date filter from the URL via `$derived(readDateFilter($page.url.searchParams))` using the **legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store**. That is the same pattern that broke the Spending year selector: the store doesn't reliably re-track inside `$derived` across a remount, so after navigating away and pressing **Back** the URL can say one date range while the page renders another. Spending was fixed by reading the year in a **`+page.ts` `load`** (`data.year`) with the arrows using **`goto`** — `load` re-runs with the right URL on every navigation. (Client-side derivation did NOT hold up: both `$app/stores` `$page` and the `$app/state` reactive `page` went stale on Back.) Apply the same `load`-based pattern here, and audit any other `$derived(… $page.url …)` site. Latent — not yet reproduced for expenses.
- **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished.** `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected, populated, and unit-tested, but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced but never built. **Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.**
- **Watch for storage-policy drift.** `supabase db dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are hand-maintained at the end of `20260726120000_baseline.sql`. A future storage change written only as a migration will be lost the next time the baseline is regenerated; one made only in the dashboard will never reach a new environment. Consider a check that diffs live storage policies against the baseline.
- **Manually verify `ReceiptImageViewer` gestures.** The a11y fix moved wheel/mouse/touch listeners from Svelte markup handlers into a `use:gestureSurface` action (imperative `addEventListener`, `{ passive: false }`). Unit tests cover logic, not real gestures — manually confirm wheel-zoom, drag-to-pan, pinch-zoom, and keyboard/screen-reader access still work.
- **PRD correction: Resend "no receipt" status is 422, not 404.** The testability PRD's §5 test plan lists `404` for the nothing-found-anywhere row, but the deployed handler returns `422` — `404` is reserved for the unknown-sender case. The tests assert the real `422`; the PRD table is the doc that's wrong. Low priority: fix the table or leave the note.

## Refactoring

No open items. Every catalogued refactoring (**RF-01→13**, plus code-review
follow-ups **RV-01→11**) has landed — see [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md)
for the per-item Landed notes. The only outstanding entries are the two deferred
value-object questions, **RF-D1** (`Money`) and **RF-D2** (typed date) — both a
recorded _keep-primitives_ decision, not scheduled work. New refactoring ideas start
here as one-liners and get promoted to an `RF-NN` entry only when work begins.

## Open questions

- **Combining receipts for one expense.** How to handle when two receipts should be combined into one expense to match — e.g. two medications picked up at the same time.
- **WealthSimple refund handling.** WealthSimple records several rows when a refund is issued. Example:

  ```csv
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-24","Refund initiated","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","33.9","CAD"
  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
  ```

- **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. - **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). - **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.

Done. `docs/product-backlog.md`: **59 bullets → 28**, **6,163 → 2,186 words**. Prettier clean, all 10 internal links resolve.

## What I extracted before deleting

Five durable lessons were only recorded inside DONE bullets. They now live where they'll actually be read:

**→ `CLAUDE.md` Gotchas** (5 new entries):
- **Supabase `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` doesn't remove `anon`/`authenticated`** — they hold *direct* grants via default privileges. A function can look locked down and still be anon-executable.
- **PostgREST's silent 1000-row cap** — page with `.range()`, and count with an exact `head` count, never a plain select's `.length`. This one had already caused a real bug twice.
- **Regenerating `.svelte-kit` drops the root `tsconfig` `include` additions** — the reason `scripts/` and `e2e/` are type-checked at all.
- **`.env` is a FIFO** — nothing can read it twice; explains the Playwright hard-coded config.
- **Test harness locations** — `appMocks.ts`, `supabaseMock.ts`, `rowBuilders.ts`, `fetchMock.ts`, plus the audit heuristic: look for logic reimplemented *inline inside `it()` bodies*, not just `function`-defined helpers.

**→ `docs/demo-seed.md`**: the `teardownDemo()` ordering trap (must delete auth users **before** the family — `receipts.family_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, receipts only cascade via `user_id`). This was the one lesson with no other home; ADR-0004 and `local-dev.md` already covered the waterfall salvage note and the migration squash, so those bullets were safe to drop outright.

## One still-open item was hiding under a ✅

The seed-function lockdown bullet ended with *"Still open: a sweep of any other `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE."* That's now its own open Security bullet rather than a footnote on a checked-off item.

- Engineering split into **In progress / Security / Dependencies / Correctness & infrastructure** — it was a 26-item flat wall.
- Deleted the now-empty **Test-coverage backlog** and **Test-suite cleanup** subsections (all 16 items done).
- Header now states the convention: *completed work is deleted, not annotated.*
- Fixed the dangling "see View family members above" reference in the Family editor bullet.
